items.title: How Much Upside Can APP Stock's Growth Deliver?
items.summary: While known for gaming, the company's fastest growth is happening elsewhere. Its consumer vertical is quietly becoming a second engine, with advertiser spend already setting records. This segment finished the second quarter 28% above fourth quarter 2025 levels.

items.title: AppLovin Stock: Is APP Underperforming the Communication Services Sector?
items.summary: AppLovin has notably underperformed the Communication Services sector over the past year, but analysts are highly optimistic about the stock’s prospects.

items.title: Can The Trade Desk's JBPs Become Its Next Major Growth Engine?
items.summary: TTD's fast-growing JBPs are emerging as a key growth lever as macro pressures weigh on near-term performance.

items.title: AppLovin’s Algorithmic Moat Is Vulnerable, Says Investor: Why $1.9B Quarterly Revenue Isn’t Enough to Justify a Buy
items.summary: AppLovin prints $1.9 billion quarters and 84% margins, yet two disciplined investors studied the model and walked away. Their reason cuts to the heart of what separates a durable moat from a very good algorithm.

items.title: Why The Trade Desk Stock Rallied Today
items.summary: The programmatic advertising specialist finally got some good news.

items.title: Magnite Rallies 6%, Trade Desk Climbs 5%, AppLovin Barely Budges: Is Agentic Ad-Tech Broadening Out?
items.summary: Magnite and Trade Desk are surging while AppLovin sits perfectly still, and the reason points to a fault line forming inside programmatic advertising that could reshape how investors price all three stocks.

items.title: Why The Trade Desk Stock Lost 24% in August
items.summary: The adtech company turned in another disastrous earnings report.

items.title: Trade Desk Rises 5% on Kokai Zuma Agentic AI Launch, AppLovin and Magnite Barely Budge
items.summary: Kokai Zuma just handed The Trade Desk a rare green day in a brutal year, but two rivals with equally loud AI launches barely moved. The divergence reveals how differently Wall Street is grading the same playbook across ad tech right now.
